## The words

| word | code | kind | is | test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **candidate** (inside **scan**) | `scan.candidate` | core | a recurring declared name with no word — vocabulary the codebase is asking for | what wants a definition |
| **code** (inside **ontology**) | `onto.code` | core | a word's dotted address (har, har.cell) — prefixes must resolve to words, so the namespace stays a tree | where a word lives |
| **collision** (inside **scan**) | `scan.collision` | core | a declaration named after a word that means something else — the failure scan exists to catch | where code and vocabulary disagree |
| **doctrine** (inside **ontology**) | `onto.doctrine` | core | a decision written down in the database — because a decision that is not written down gets re-litigated | why it is this way |
| **drift** (inside **scan**) | `scan.drift` | core | a value or prose that moved away from the vocabulary it claims: a rogue literal, a near-duplicate, a stale render | what the gate exists to catch |
| **migration** (inside **scan**) | `scan.migration` | core | a renamed word propagated through the code by token — sweep reports, apply rewrites, the diff is the review | how the code catches up |
| **ontology** | `onto` | core | a repo's vocabulary as a database: words, doctrine, rulings — enforced by scan, rendered to prose, never authored in prose | what the words are |
| **ruling** (inside **ontology**) | `onto.ruling` | core | a recorded boundary decision: an overload (say Y not X), a collision (whose word it is, who moved), or a rename (was, now, why) | how arguments end |
| **scan** | `scan` | core | the tree-sitter sweep of a codebase: every declaration measured, checked against the vocabulary | what the code claims |
| **sync** (inside **ontology**) | `onto.sync` | core | rendering the database to the generated words skill — prose is output, never source | how agents read it |
| **token** (inside **ontology**) | `onto.token` | core | a named design value — color, space, radius, shadow, font, breakpoint — the vocabulary a visual system trades in | what design means |
| **word** (inside **ontology**) | `onto.word` | core | one term with one meaning: definition, the one-line test, an optional owner and dotted code | what we mean |
| **workspace** | `ws` | core | any repo montology is initialized into — found by walking up for .monty, the way git finds .git | where work happens |

## Prose is rendered, never authored

The database is the truth. The words skill, the CLAUDE.md section, any listing — all render FROM it (`monty sync`). A vocabulary kept in prose stays correct only as long as someone remembers to keep it correct; the last one drifted, which is why this one is a database with a gate.

## The gate is the point

`monty lint` fails a build: collisions (a declaration named after a word that means something else), unresolvable code prefixes, generated prose gone stale behind the database. Errors carry the repair. An ontology without enforcement is a glossary.

## Rules

1. Before naming ANYTHING — a class, a concept, a tag: `monty onto check <name>`.
2. A word means one thing. If it cannot, pick a different word.
3. Vendors are not vocabulary — tools you buy belong in code, never in a
   sentence about what the system means.
4. A dotted code lives inside the word owning its prefix.
